prerequisites: Average programming skills in a high level programming language

learning_outcomes.text: The graduate has knowledge related to programming, mathematics, engineering and technology and has the skills to use them to create complex information technology systems.
The graduate has the knowledge to select and use appropriate instructional procedures to facilitate the process of knowledge assimilation.
The graduate is able to present and explain methods, algorithms, paradigms and techniques used in various branches of computer science.
The graduate is able to identify complex problems and examine related issues to develop solving options and implement solutions.
The graduate is able to combine diverse information to formulate solutions and generate ideas for developing new products and applications.
The graduate has the ability to apply general rules to specific problems and produce relevant solutions.

The graduate has the ability to choose and use programming paradigms (procedural, object-oriented, functional) to develop software applications appropriate for the specific domain of the application being developed.
Advanced programming skills in high-level programming languages.
Use of theoretical foundations of computer science as well as of formal models.
Application to specific field, to organize and create effective tools and to evaluate work rules, principles and norms.

Use of efficient methods and techniques to learn, inform, research and develop the abilities to bring value to knowledge, to adapt at the requirements of a dynamical society and to communicate efficiently in Romanian language and in an international language.
Be able to understand compiler design and to implement compiler techniques.
Acquire knowledge about back-end of a compiler.

Understand and work with formal languages concepts: Chomsky hierarchy; regular grammars, finite automata and the equivalence between them; context-free grammars, push-down automata and their equivalence.
Understand and work with compilers concepts: scanning, parsing.

assessment_methods.method: Practical examination during all semester / documentation / portfolio

assessment_rules: To pass, students must attend 75% of seminar activities and 90% of lab activities. A minimum grade of 5 (on a scale of 1 to 10) is required for both the written exam and the laboratory work. Students must also understand basic concepts of formal languages, including grammars and finite automata, and be able to apply scanning and parsing algorithms.
